openings.claim: Unrecorded compatibility and inherited 90-minute blocks may hide feasible access.
openings.discriminator: Compare existing allocation, needs-matched allocation, and 60-minute entitlements followed by extensions; nominal vacancies and entitlements do not establish full needs coverage.
openings.probe: Interview contacts about needs, windows, equipment and useful durations; compare paper allocations and administration before agreed changes.
openings.uncertainty: Usable alternatives, beneficial shortening and target feasibility remain unknown.

openings.claim: One desk-authoritative ledger and replacement confirmations may reduce contradictory access expectations.
openings.discriminator: Fewer stale or duplicate confirmations, weighed against logging time.
openings.probe: Pilot unique references, room/date/time and superseded-reference readback, and online synchronization timestamps; log conflict causes and all administration for eight weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Consistent consultation is required; two conflicts have unexplained causes.

openings.claim: Shared indispensable musicians may make separate bookings mutually unusable.
openings.discriminator: Group-pair attendance conflicts explain affected late or missed sessions.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints with an accepted exchange.
openings.probe: Ask contacts about essential-member overlap in the 14 affected sessions; record group pairs only. If supported, trial one acceptable exchange and compare attendance.
openings.uncertainty: Overlap and an acceptable exchange are unobserved.

lineage.reason: With Z1; retains entitlement-first fragmentation hypothesis.

decision: Probe feasibility before allocation changes. Preserve two rooms, 24 staffed hours, every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement, offline channels, equipment, zero new fees and both performances. Test eight-week coverage >=90%, conflicts <2 and administration <=120 minutes/week; success is unestablished.
